original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: One replay stage: the exact rational nesting stage of make verify-recycled-bit (recycled-bit-integration/verify.py --all), whose Exact init and per-move basis/annihilator work is dominated by PR97 linalg.null_exact (Fraction RREF). Replace that kernel (and frames147.prim) at runtime by an output-identical fraction-free integer kernel, with an in-tree audit mode and before/after timing on the same pinned input.
scope_change_reason: Refined from the card's generic "profile one replay" to one measured stage. The first mechanism (seed the basis memo from check_lifted.late_frames' discarded exact_basis cache) was refuted by measurement: the cache covers 2,230 of 86,789 distinct ledger-move keys (2.6%). One evidence-driven pivot to the dominant measured kernel (about 72% of per-move cost) with an identical-output requirement.
bottleneck_link: verify-recycled-bit is the longest verify.yml job (657 s on main run 38506758315, 619 s in this stage); a faster identical replay shortens review/CI turnaround for every PR that runs it and for make verify. It is a side result for the kappa bottleneck: no mathematical change.
stop_rule: Stop and submit a profiling note instead of a code change if the fast kernel gives < 1.5x on the sampled basis+null workload, if any output differs from the reference null_exact, or if the full after-run cannot finish by 2026-10-15T13:40:15Z (then report subset-only results).
evidence: Same host, same pinned input: init audit 4,473 null_exact calls identical (kernel 23.43 s -> 2.88 s); 400-move sample basis+null 4.50/3.88 s -> 1.25/1.11 s with identical maps; complete full-key audit 145,513 null_exact + 1,683,853 prim calls identical (381.0 s -> 48.7 s; 70.6 s -> 3.6 s); full --all with VERIFY_JOBS=3: nesting stage 410 s -> 226 s wall, about 1.44-1.81x from one before/after pair on a loaded host, before-run = VERIFY_NULL=reference on the patched file (whole run 427.7 s -> 243.5 s; user CPU 825 s -> 369 s), same five PASS lines and kappa, certificate equal. Bounded package check with negative controls: research/recycled-bit-nesting-reuse/verify.py. CI wall time not measured.

open_questions.question: Can Frames.dims (mod-p Echelon rank in check_lifted) be made faster with identical ranks?
open_questions.why_it_matters: After this change it is the largest serial part of Exact.__init__, paid before the worker pool starts.
open_questions.first_step: Install a packed or batched mod-Q31 elimination behind the same runtime-install/audit pattern and audit all 112,920 _rank calls.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing; needs its own equality audit.

open_questions.question: Should the parent build shared source-key bases once before forking the pool?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Workers rebuild overlapping source-key bases; copy-on-write sharing removes the duplicate work.
open_questions.first_step: Measure source-key overlap across the current chunks and the parent RSS for prebuilt bases.
open_questions.blocked_by: Memory on CI runners if all 86,789 bases are prebuilt.

open_questions.question: Do bit-reuse-147 and gauge-recycling replays, which also use PR97 null_exact via frames147.Exact, benefit from the same installer?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The kernel is shared, so the same identical-output speedup may apply.
open_questions.first_step: Profile make verify-bit-reuse-147 and measure its null_exact share.
open_questions.blocked_by: Each verifier pins its own sources and needs its own pin update and review.
